legend: Multiple firm and ulcerative skin nodules on the forearm.
The tumour typically exhibits a nodular architecture with extensive geographical necrosis (i.e. pseudogranulomatous pattern).

Neoplastic nodules are composed of an admixture of epithelioid and spindle cells. Tumour cells infiltrate the dermal collagen and show a pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, indistinct cell borders, and moderate nuclear atypia.
At times, epithelioid sarcoma is composed predominantly of spindle cells.
Perineural and intraneural growth is often seen in epithelioid sarcoma.
Neoplastic cells feature marked cytological atypia and assume a carcinoma-like morphology. Vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and abundant mitotic figures are seen.
The tumour exhibits eosinophilic hyaline (rhabdoid) cytoplasmic inclusions.
Diffuse pancytokeratin immunopositivity is seen in the vast majority of cases.
CD34 immunopositivity is observed in approximately 50% of both classic and proximal epithelioid sarcoma.
Loss of nuclear expression of SMARCB1 (INI1) is almost invariably seen in both classic and proximal epithelioid sarcomas.
Tumour is composed of partly anastomosing solid sheets and nests of large pleomorphic epithelioid cells that have deeply eosinophilic cytoplasm and pleomorphic nuclei.
source: Dr Jennifer Brown & Dr Zsolt Orosz, Department of Pathology, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford University Hospitals, UK

legend: Axial 18F-FDG PET/CT, fat-saturated T1-weighted imaging (pre-contrast, shown here, and postcontrast, Fig. <<56703>>), and T2-weighted imaging (Fig. <<56704>>) of an epithelioid sarcoma in the right perineum. This demonstrates marked inhomogeneous 18F-FDG avidity, T1 isointensity to muscle, with avid inhomogeneous postcontrast enhancement, and variably elevated T2 hyperintensity. These lesions are often inhomogeneous due to the varying degrees of necrosis and as such may have variable signal patterns (Fig: <<56705>>).
source: Dr Huw Walters and Dr Rajat Chowdhury, Department of Radiology, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford University Hospitals, UK
